source: Quiz 5 - Sessions 1-6: Model Training, Alignment, and the Agent Harness
question: Why might a base model continue a request as part of a document instead of answering helpfully?

options.text: A base model has already optimized each reply for a user preference score
options.feedback: Optimizing with a reward signal is part of a classic post-training pipeline. It does not describe a base model after foundational prediction training.

options.text: Its objective teaches continuation, not reliable assistance
options.feedback: Predicting what text comes next can support document continuation. Further training helps shape reliable assistant-style responses.

options.text: Its foundational objective teaches refusal instead of language prediction
options.feedback: Refusal of harmful requests is an example of preferred behavior encouraged later. The foundational text-model objective is prediction.

options.text: A base model lacks learned patterns needed to produce connected text
options.feedback: Pre-training can build extensive language patterns. The issue is the style and purpose of the continuation, not an absence of language learning.
